D009-D008_h004.question_both:
Alright, Doc. Thanks for seeing me. It’s been… a weird year, to say the least. For about a month, not too long ago, I was on top of the world. Everything was exciting. I felt invincible – like I could crack any system, solve any puzzle. Sleep? Who needs it when there’s so much to do, so many ideas buzzing? I was talking a mile a minute, bouncing from one thought to the next, like my brain couldn’t keep up. And my sex drive… let’s just say I was making up for lost time. Honestly, it was great, and I was still getting my work done, maybe even better than usual.

But then that fizzled out, and for the last year, it’s been… this. I just feel so incredibly flat. Like all the color drained out of everything. Socializing? Forget it. My friends try to get me out, but it just feels like too much effort to pretend to care. My brain feels like it's wading through mud; even basic coding takes forever. Sometimes, out of nowhere, I get this really unsettling urge, like wanting to step in front of traffic or jump off a tall building, just a fleeting thought, but it scares me. It's really messed with my work, and honestly, just getting out of bed feels like a colossal achievement some days.

My mind was racing, and I couldn't stop talking – my friends were probably exhausted trying to keep up. I also noticed a big uptick in my sex drive, which was… different. But honestly, it didn't mess up my work or anything. If anything, I felt more productive.

That lasted about a month. But for the past year, it's been a completely different story. I feel this emptiness, like my emotions are just gone. I don't want to see anyone, and even thinking feels like a monumental effort. It’s like my brain just shuts down after a few minutes. Sometimes, these really alarming thoughts pop into my head – urges to just step in front of a car or jump off something high, even though I know I’d never actually act on them. This part has really impacted my ability to do my job; I’m barely keeping up. The intense highs don't cause any real problems, and I definitely haven’t experienced anything like losing touch with reality. It’s the lows that are truly debilitating.

Maybe I’m just overthinking things.

Nothing brings me joy anymore, not even watching the games or messing with my truck. My wife, bless her heart, she tries to talk to me, but I just can’t focus. Sometimes, I even think about just… ending it all, how I could do it during my long hauls, make it look like an accident.

I was snapping at everyone, even other drivers for little things that wouldn’t normally bother me. I started planning out all these extra side jobs, thinking I could get them all done, even though I knew I barely had time for my regular load. My wife said I was manic, but I just felt wired, buzzing. But even then, I couldn’t stick to one task. I'd be trying to fix a part, then remember something else I needed to do, and just jump to that. Now I feel like I'm sinking back into that dark place again."

Nothing really caught my interest, not even my fishing pole. My wife tried to talk to me, but I couldn't focus; my mind just drifted. I'd feel this crushing guilt, like every little problem at home was my fault, like I deserved to be punished. Sometimes, I even started thinking about how I could just end it, picturing how it might happen. That pretty much shut me down; I could barely get my shifts in.

Then, about three weeks ago, something shifted. I felt a surge of energy, like I could take on the world. I started cleaning out the garage, then decided to rebuild the old pickup, and then completely re-route all my deliveries for maximum efficiency – all at once. My wife said I was being impossible, snapping at her over little things, and I guess I was a bit irritable. I’d try to concentrate on my logbook, but my mind was constantly jumping; I couldn't stick with anything for long. But even with all that, I was still driving my routes, getting my work done, and managing things at home. It’s not like I needed to be locked up, and I wasn't hearing voices or anything; I was just… on a different wavelength.

I was barely sleeping, maybe two or three hours a night, but I still had tons of energy. My wife said I was being really short-tempered, easily getting angry over little things that wouldn't normally bother me. I was so amped up, trying to fix up the house, plan new routes for work, and even starting a garden, all at once. My mind was just zipping from one thing to another, I couldn't focus on any one task for long. It wasn't causing problems at work, though; I was still getting my deliveries done.

But then, about four months ago, it all came crashing down. I just feel… empty. Like there’s nothing inside me. The routes I used to love, the open road – they just don't do anything for me anymore. My wife tries to get me to watch a movie or hang out with old friends, but I just can’t get into it. Everything feels pointless. It’s even hard to follow a conversation or read a simple newspaper article; my mind just drifts. And the guilt… I feel responsible for everything, like if I don't call my mother-in-law often enough, something bad will happen. I even find myself thinking about driving off a cliff somewhere quiet, picturing exactly how it would happen and where. This whole thing has messed me up badly, to the point where I've had to take time off from driving.
